meta.primaryEquation: Eq.3 (Escalation threshold: E* = E + m*c - Ps)
meta.strategicSummary: Day 28 of the Hormuz closure sees a decisive shift in Gulf state posture: Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Bahrain have moved from passive beneficiaries of Iranian pressure to active advocates for expanded US military operations. MBS framing the crisis as a 'historic opportunity' removes the most important potential Arab de-escalation broker, materially raising the base escalation cost E to 6. The UAE's emerging operational role strengthens the US coalition guarantee (Ps rises to 14), while the food/fertilizer supply chain disruption at day 28 signals that the global economic damage is now transmitting beyond energy markets into systemic commodity shocks — increasing international urgency but not yet changing structural model parameters. Credibility c ticks up modestly as the sustained multi-actor pressure environment makes any near-term Iranian capitulation less likely. The mediator channel remains nominally open but is under increasing strain as Gulf states actively push for attacks rather than negotiation.
meta.mostSignificantEvent: Headline 4 (UAE/Saudi/Bahrain urging US to ramp up Iran attacks): This trilateral demand is the most consequential because it transforms three of the largest regional stakeholders from potential pressure-for-ceasefire actors into active escalation advocates, eliminates a key diplomatic off-ramp, directly drives Ps upward, and confirms E should move to 6 — fundamentally reshaping the coalition architecture of the conflict.

news.headline: Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman is said to view US-Israeli war as ‘historic opportunity’ to remake Middle East.

metricsImpact.note: MBS 'historic opportunity' framing is the most geopolitically destabilizing signal — it suggests Saudi Arabia will not push for a quick ceasefire, removing a key de-escalation actor and raising the probability of a wider regional war that raises E from 5 to 6.

news.headline: The disruption is now affecting not only energy but also global food supply chains. A significant portion of fertilizer trade and LNG flows passing through the Strait of Hormuz has been impacted, raising concerns about broader economic consequences

metricsImpact.E_delta: +0 (already captured in E=6; but food/fertilizer dimension raises international pressure on all parties)
metricsImpact.m_note: m_base unchanged — fertilizer/LNG disruption is a downstream effect of existing closure, not a new strait event
metricsImpact.note: Food supply chain contagion broadens the economic damage narrative, increasing international pressure for resolution but also raising the stakes for Iran's coercive leverage; does not mechanically change m but strengthens the political economy case for a higher effective multiplier over time.

paramNotes.dual_strait: Binary flag: 0 = Hormuz-only scenario; 1 = dual-strait activation (Hormuz + Bab-el-Mandeb via Houthi proxy). When 1, m switches from m_base to m_activated.
paramNotes.m_base: Geographic multiplier when only Hormuz is threatened (~20% global oil). Default 3.0.
paramNotes.m_activated: Geographic multiplier when both Hormuz and Bab-el-Mandeb (Houthi proxy) are simultaneously threatened (~30% global oil + Red Sea disruption). Default 4.75.
paramNotes.mediator_status: Binary flag: 1 = Qatar/Oman back-channel operative (sanctions-relief pathway open); 0 = mediator pathway closed (IRGC strike on Qatari/Omani assets or diplomatic rupture). When 0, Sr is gated — cannot rise regardless of diplomatic signals.
